exercises.prompt: After a long walk, how do you say **My feet hurt**?
hints: *Doler* works like *gustar*: the thing that hurts is the subject.
*Los pies* is plural, and Spanish uses *the*, not *my*, with body parts.

options.label: Me duelen los pies.
options.feedback: Yes: plural subject (*los pies*), so *duelen*; *me* says whose feet.

options.label: Me duele los pies.
options.feedback: Not yet — the verb agrees with *los pies*, which is plural: *duelen*.

options.label: Me duelen mis pies.
options.feedback: Not yet — with body parts Spanish uses the article: *los pies*. The *me* already shows they're yours.

options.label: Duelo los pies.
options.feedback: Not yet — *doler* isn't used like that. The feet are the subject: *Me duelen los pies*.

exercises.solution: **Me duelen los pies.** Like *gustar*, *doler* agrees with the thing that hurts (*los pies*, plural → *duelen*), and the person is shown by *me, te, le…*. Body parts take *the*, not *my*.

hints: Use *doler*: "the head hurts me".
*Me duele* + *la cabeza*.
answers: A mí me duele la cabeza

feedback.message: Almost — with body parts, use the article: *Me duele la cabeza*.
Not quite! That says "I have a head". Try *Me duele la cabeza*.

exercises.solution: **Me duele la cabeza** (or *Tengo dolor de cabeza*). With *doler*, the head is the subject and *me* shows whose it is; the article *la* replaces English "my".

exercises.prompt: Ask a friend what hurts: *¿Qué ___ duele?* (Type only the missing word.)
hints: You need the pronoun for "to you" with a friend.
Same pronoun as in *¿Te gusta…?*

feedback.message: That's correct for *usted* (or for him/her). For a friend: *te*.
Almost — with *doler*, use the object pronoun *te*, not the subject pronoun *tú*.

exercises.solution: **te**: *¿Qué te duele?* (What hurts?) Formally: *¿Qué le duele?*

exercises.prompt: Give a friend an affirmative **tú** command with **beber**: *¡___ mucha agua!*
hints: For regular verbs, the *tú* command is the same as the *él/ella* form of the present.
*Él bebe* → *¡…!*

feedback.message: Almost — *bebes* is a statement ("you drink"). The command drops the -s: *bebe*.
That's the *usted* command. For a friend: *bebe*.

exercises.solution: **Bebe** mucha agua. The affirmative *tú* command of a regular verb looks like the *él/ella* form of the present: *bebe, toma, abre*.

exercises.prompt: Tell a child to come here: *¡___ aquí!* (venir, tú)
hints: *Venir* is one of the eight irregular *tú* commands.
The others are *di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten*.

feedback.message: Almost — *venir* has a short irregular command: *ven*.
That's the *usted* command (also used as "come on!" in Spain). For a child: *ven*.

exercises.solution: **Ven** aquí. The eight irregular *tú* commands are *di* (decir), *haz* (hacer), *ve* (ir), *pon* (poner), *sal* (salir), *sé* (ser), *ten* (tener), *ven* (venir).

exercises.prompt: Tell your younger brother to do his homework: *___ los deberes.* (hacer, tú)
hints: *Hacer* has an irregular, one-syllable *tú* command.
It ends in *z*.

feedback.message: Almost — *hace* is "he does". The command is irregular: *haz*.
Almost — the command of *hacer* is spelled with *z*: *haz*.

exercises.solution: **Haz** los deberes. *Hacer → haz*. (In Latin America, homework is also *la tarea*: *Haz la tarea*.)

exercises.prompt: Make a negative **tú** command with **hablar**: *No ___ tan alto, por favor.* (Don't talk so loudly.)
hints: Start from the *yo* form, *hablo*, and drop the -o.
-ar verbs take the "opposite" ending *-es*.

feedback.message: Almost — *no hablas* is a statement ("you don't talk"). The negative command switches the vowel: *no hables*.
Almost — the affirmative form doesn't work with *no*. Negative command: *no hables*.

exercises.solution: **hables**: *No hables tan alto, por favor.* *hablo → habl- → hables*. -ar verbs take *-es*, -er/-ir verbs take *-as* (*no comas, no escribas*).

exercises.prompt: Make a negative **tú** command with **ir**: *No ___ a clase mañana, descansa.*
hints: *Ir* is one of the three negative commands you have to learn separately.
The others are *no seas* (ser) and *no estés* (estar).

feedback.message: Almost — *ve* is the affirmative command. The negative is *no vayas*.
Almost — *no vas* is a statement. The negative command is *no vayas*.
Close — the form is irregular: *vayas*.

exercises.solution: **vayas**: *No vayas a clase mañana, descansa.* *Ir* doesn't follow the *yo*-form rule (*voy*), so learn it: *no vayas*. Its *usted* form is *vaya*.

exercises.prompt: A doctor to a patient (**usted**): *___ estas pastillas tres veces al día.* (tomar)
hints: The *usted* command is the negative *tú* form without the -s.
*no tomes* → …

feedback.message: That's the *tú* command. A doctor speaking to a patient as *usted* says *tome*.
Almost — drop the -s for *usted*: *tome*.

exercises.solution: **Tome** estas pastillas tres veces al día. *Tomar*: *yo tomo → tom- → tome*. -ar verbs switch to *e* in the *usted* command; -er/-ir verbs switch to *a* (*beba, abra*).

exercises.prompt: A receptionist asks a visitor (**usted**) to sit down: *___, por favor.* (sentarse)
hints: *Sentarse* is e → ie and reflexive. The *usted* command of *sentar* is *siente*.
Attach the *usted* pronoun *se*, and add a written accent to keep the stress.

feedback.message: That's the *tú* command. For *usted*: *siéntese*.
Almost — in an affirmative command, the pronoun is attached to the end: *siéntese*.
Almost — the stress stays on *SIEN*, three syllables from the end, so it needs an accent: *siéntese*.

exercises.solution: **Siéntese**, por favor. *Sentarse* → *usted* command *siente* (with the stem change) + *se* attached. The stressed syllable is now third from the end, so it needs a written accent. To a friend: *siéntate*.

exercises.prompt: Your friend is exhausted. How do you tell her **Go to bed!** (acostarse, tú)?
hints: Affirmative command: the pronoun is attached to the end.
*Acostarse* is o → ue, and the stress stays on *-cues-*.

options.label: ¡Acuéstate!
options.feedback: Yes: *acuesta* + *te*, with an accent to keep the stress.

options.label: ¡Te acuestas!
options.feedback: Not yet — that's a statement ("you go to bed"). In an affirmative command, attach the pronoun: *acuéstate*.

options.label: ¡No te acuestes!
options.feedback: Not yet — that's the negative: "Don't go to bed!".

options.label: ¡Acuéstese!
options.feedback: Close, but that's the *usted* command. To a friend: *acuéstate*.

exercises.solution: **¡Acuéstate!** The *tú* command *acuesta* (with the stem change, like *él acuesta*) + *te* attached; the accent keeps the stress on *-cues-*. Negative: *¡No te acuestes!* To *usted*: *¡Acuéstese!* (With *vos*: *¡Acostate!*)

hints: It's a negative command, so the pronoun goes before the verb.
*preocupo → preocup- → -es*, with *te*.

feedback.message: That's perfect for *usted*. To a friend: *No te preocupes*.
Almost — in negative commands, the pronoun goes before the verb, and the form changes: *No te preocupes*.
Almost — that's a statement. The negative command: *No te preocupes*.

exercises.solution: **No te preocupes.** Negative *tú* command: from *preocupo* → *preocup-* + *-es*, with the pronoun *te* before the verb. To *usted*: *No se preocupe*.
